name: Account compromise
rationale: No direct evidence of unauthorized logins or sessions exists in the local code or environment config, but live session logs on Google are currently UNKNOWN.

name: OAuth compromise
rationale: The application uses local App Passwords for SMTP. Google OAuth client IDs and scopes are clean locally, but live console grants are UNKNOWN.

name: Malicious/unsafe browser extension
rationale: No browser extension audits can be completed programmatically by the agent.

name: Bulk sending
rationale: The microservices architecture triggers automated transactional emails for order placement, confirmation, shipping, delivery, returns, and payment events. Developer testing or seeding cycles create bulk sending volume.

name: Unsolicited email
rationale: If local testing used placeholder customer addresses, these would result in high bounce rates, which Google flags as spam activity.

name: Job-application automation
rationale: No job application automation libraries or configs are present in the repository.

name: Automation misconfiguration
rationale: The application lacks sandbox controls, sends actual emails in development/testing environments, and records optimistic 'SENT' status in database logs, obscuring SMTP transport errors.

name: Excessive sending frequency
rationale: Kafka listener threads trigger asynchronous email sends in parallel. Google's personal SMTP servers block high-frequency, parallel connection bursts.

name: Repeated message pattern
rationale: Sending identical welcome and order HTML email structures (only differing by order IDs/names) in close succession triggers Gmail content spam filters.

name: Recipient complaints/spam reports
rationale: Bounced emails from unverified test domains or mock users trigger automated Google abuse signals.

name: Unknown third-party integration
rationale: No unknown integrations found in local project configurations.

name: Google-side enforcement despite no local cause
rationale: A clear local cause exists: the local microservices project was configured to send transactional emails via entitykart@gmail.com with an App Password, with no rate limiters or dev-mode sandboxing.

name: Combination of multiple causes (H4 + H7 + H8 + H9)
rationale: The combination of bulk transactional sends during local testing, lack of development sandboxing/throttling, rapid-fire parallel SMTP connections via @Async, and sending identical HTML message patterns directly resulted in Google flagging the personal account as a spam transmitter.
